zh.summary: 從郵件角色、傳遞紀錄與網域驗證，建立清楚可查核的郵件足跡。

sourceBody.text: CEH M02-05｜電子郵件足跡：讀懂寄送路徑與網域驗證
1｜先記住這個結論
電子郵件足跡蒐集（Email Footprinting）是從公開的聯絡資訊，以及自己有權查看的郵件原始資料，整理寄件網域、郵件服務、傳遞路徑與驗證結果。把這些線索放在一起，就能回答：「這封信經過哪些系統？使用哪個網域寄送？收件端做過哪些檢查？」
本課接續 M02-04 的 DNS：DNS 的 MX 紀錄協助找到收信服務；這次往下一層，閱讀一封信真正留下的資料。也呼應 M09 的反釣魚觀念：技術驗證協助確認網域與傳遞，重要業務要求則透過既有聯絡管道確認。
用一句話記住分工：信封負責投遞，標頭描述郵件，收件系統提供路徑與驗證證據。以下全部使用合成案例與 .example 教學網域，練習範圍是離線判讀。
2｜先用寄包裹理解電子郵件
你寄一個包裹時，有包裹外的物流單，也有包裹內的信。電子郵件同樣有兩層資料。
Envelope（郵件信封）是系統投遞時使用的資訊。SMTP（Simple Mail Transfer Protocol，簡單郵件傳輸協定）的 MAIL FROM 提供退信路徑，RCPT TO 指定實際投遞對象。Header（郵件標頭）是信件本身開頭的欄位；使用者看到的 From、To、Subject 就在這一層。Body（本文）則是文字與附加內容。

像活動平台代咖啡店寄收據：畫面 From 可以是 receipt@coffee.example，退信則交給 bounce@mailer.example 處理。兩個地址各有職責；判讀時先把角色標清楚。密件副本 Bcc 也能幫助理解：收件人可能已列入投遞信封，而畫面上的 To 欄保持另一份清單。[SMTP 信封與傳輸規範](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321)、[郵件格式規範](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5322)
常見寄送流程是：寄件人的郵件軟體 → 提交服務 → 一個或多個轉送伺服器 → 收件伺服器 → 收件人的郵件軟體。轉送伺服器稱為 MTA（Mail Transfer Agent，郵件傳輸代理），每一站把信交給下一站。Webmail（網頁信箱）則讓使用者透過網站操作信箱。[網際網路郵件架構](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5598)

連接埠可以當作服務入口編號來記：SMTP 伺服器間傳遞常見 TCP 25；使用者提交郵件常見 587，或使用隱式 TLS 的 465。TLS（Transport Layer Security，傳輸層安全協定）保護連線中的資料。IMAP（Internet Message Access Protocol，網際網路郵件存取協定）供郵件軟體讀取及同步信箱，隱式 TLS 常見 993；網頁信箱通常透過 HTTPS 443。看到入口編號後，再配合服務設定確認用途。[郵件提交與存取的 TLS 建議](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8314)

sourceBody.text: 3｜開啟原始郵件：每個欄位回答一種問題
在 Gmail 網頁版，開啟自己收到的郵件，從回覆旁的更多選單選「顯示原始郵件」，可以查看完整標頭。其他郵件軟體可能稱為「檢視來源」或「完整標頭」。分析時保留原始檔，另製作遮蔽個資的工作副本。[Gmail 官方步驟](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/29436?hl=en)
• From：信件所呈現的作者地址；Display Name（顯示名稱）是旁邊方便人閱讀的名稱。先讀完整地址，再看其網域。
• Reply-To：按下回覆時建議使用的地址；客服平台、代寄或工單服務可能使用獨立回覆地址，適合與實際業務流程核對。
• To／Cc：信件呈現的主要收件人與副本收件人。
• Return-Path：最終投遞時記錄的退信路徑，可協助對照 SMTP 信封。
• Date：郵件中標示的建立日期；與收件時間比較時，一併保留時區。
• Message-ID：訊息識別碼，可作為搜尋與比對日誌的線索；有些系統另外提供自己的內部郵件 ID，記錄時分開保存。
• Received：傳遞節點留下的接收紀錄，是重建寄送路徑的主要材料。
• Authentication-Results：驗證服務記錄的檢查結果，通常包含 SPF、DKIM、DMARC。[郵件欄位](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5322)、[驗證結果標頭](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8601)
公開聯絡頁上的 info@、support@ 等角色信箱，以及郵件簽名檔中的部門與聯絡方式，也能提供組織足跡。整理時只收與任務相關的欄位，並把「公開頁面資料」與「已取得郵件的技術資料」分開列出。這延續 M02-02 的來源查證：每個欄位都帶著自己的來源與時間。
4｜Received 怎麼讀：先確認可信節點，再還原時間順序
Received 回答「信經過哪些接收節點」，SPF、DKIM、DMARC 則回答「寄送來源、簽署網域與畫面作者如何對照」。先把兩類問題分開，再把證據接起來，閱讀完整郵件就有了清楚順序。
4.1 用物流配送理解接收紀錄
想像從台北寄出的包裹，依序經過寄件站、轉運站、收件站。每到一站，該站都寫下：「我在什麼時間，從哪個上一站收到包裹。」郵件伺服器（Mail Server）也會留下這類交接紀錄。Received 是寫在郵件標頭（Header）中的接收欄位；負責轉送的系統稱為 MTA（Mail Transfer Agent，郵件傳輸代理）。

rows: Received
一筆接收事件，先確認由哪個系統寫入。
from outbound.mailer.example
上一站的名稱資訊；與實際連線 IP 一起判讀。
此例中接收端記錄的連線來源 IP。
by mx.recipient.example
寫下這筆接收事件的伺服器。
該伺服器記錄的時間；+0000 表示與 UTC 相同的時差。

sourceBody.text: 若已確認這筆紀錄由可信的 mx.recipient.example 產生，可寫成：「該收件伺服器在這個時間，記錄到來自 192.0.2.25 的郵件連線。」這是節點間交接的證據。要進一步確認操作帳號與裝置，再依權限取得提交服務、登入或端點紀錄，讓每一層結論都有對應材料。[SMTP 追蹤資訊：RFC 5321 §4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321.html#section-4.4)
4.2 三站例子：時間閱讀與可信度查核各有方向
以下是同一封合成郵件的三筆接收紀錄。所有 .example 名稱與 192.0.2.x 位址都供教學使用。假設收件組織管理 mx.recipient.example 與 mailbox.recipient.example，並能查閱兩者的日誌。
新接收的伺服器會把自己的 Received 加在既有紀錄上面。於是這段標頭最上方是 10:00:10，最下方是 10:00:00。[Received 的加入方式：RFC 5321 §4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321.html#section-4.4)

rows: 還原記錄中的時間順序
由下往上，較早到較晚
查核每段紀錄的可信度
從自己的可信收件系統，逐站往前
先核對 mailbox 的內部接收，再核對 mx 的外部連線；outbound 寫下的更早資料另找服務商證據。

sourceBody.text: 先把各筆時間換成同一時區。例如 10:00:05 +0000 對應台灣 18:00:05 +0800。要估算兩站延遲，還要考慮兩台系統的時鐘同步狀態；把「標頭記載的時差」與「已核實的傳遞延遲」分開記錄，分析會更精確。
4.3 信任邊界：把每筆紀錄接回產生它的系統
信任邊界（Trust Boundary）是區分「自己可查核的系統」與「外部提供的資料」的界線。上例中，mx 直接觀察到 outbound 的連線；更早的 submit → outbound 段，則由外部系統描述。可以把證據表分成「己方日誌已對照」和「外部紀錄待對照」兩欄，再逐段補齊。
例如標頭中出現下面這行時，它首先是一項待核對的來源主張：
確認這段主張的做法，是辨識寫入者、核對可信接收鏈與相關服務日誌。信件進入可信系統以前的標頭可能由外部寄件方預先填入，因此「紀錄外觀」與「來源核驗」各自列欄。這也接回 M09 社交工程：正式名稱和熟悉招牌可以吸引信任；獨立來源與系統紀錄，則讓信任有可查核的依據。

sourceBody.text: 5｜SPF、DKIM、DMARC：三個互補的檢查
5.1 用車輛名單、文件封條與招牌對照來理解
假設郵件顯示 From: 台灣某銀行 <service@bank.example>。From 是郵件呈現的作者資訊；收件系統接著核對寄送來源與簽章，把這個名稱連到技術證據。

rows: SPF
寄送車輛的授權名單
連線來源 IP 是否符合所檢查網域的寄送政策。
DKIM
文件的數位封條
簽署網域的簽章與其涵蓋的內容是否驗證一致。
DMARC
憑證與店面招牌的對照
通過 SPF 或 DKIM 的網域，是否和 From 網域對齊。

sourceBody.text: 5.2 SPF：將來源 IP 與網域授權名單對照
SPF（Sender Policy Framework，寄件者政策框架）讓網域在 DNS（Domain Name System，網域名稱系統）公布寄送政策。TXT 是 DNS 中可放文字資料的紀錄類型。假設代寄平台使用 192.0.2.25，教學政策可寫成：
mailer.example. TXT "v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.25 -all"

v=spf1 標示 SPF 版本；ip4:192.0.2.25 列出授權的 IPv4 來源。若前面的條件都未符合，-all 讓 SPF 得到 fail 結果，表達這個網域未授權該來源；收件系統再依自己的處理政策決定拒收、標記或其他處置。[SPF fail 與處理：RFC 7208 §2.6.4、§8.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208.html#section-8.4)

收件端通常將當前連線 IP 與 SMTP（Simple Mail Transfer Protocol，簡單郵件傳輸協定）MAIL FROM 的網域比對；MAIL FROM 是投遞信封的退信身分。SPF 也定義 HELO／EHLO 身分檢查；這是 SMTP 連線的招呼名稱。分析結果時，直接寫出「哪個 IP、哪個身分、哪個網域、什麼結果」，就能和畫面上的 From 分開對照。[SPF 驗證身分：RFC 7208 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208.html#section-2)
5.3 DKIM：以公私鑰驗證簽章涵蓋的內容
DKIM（DomainKeys Identified Mail，網域金鑰識別郵件）使用非對稱式密碼學（Asymmetric Cryptography）：簽署方保管私鑰（Private Key）來產生數位簽章，收件端取得 DNS 上的公鑰（Public Key）來驗證。
以下節錄只展示需要辨識的標籤，真正的簽章另有演算法與簽章值等欄位：

rows: d=coffee.example
簽署網域；接著用它和 From 做對齊檢查。
s=selector1
Selector（選擇器），用來定位金鑰。此例查詢 selector1._domainkey.coffee.example 的 DNS TXT 紀錄。
h=from:to:subject:date
列出這個簽章選用的標頭名稱；From 必須納入簽署，驗證器依規則選取相應欄位實例。
c=relaxed/relaxed
Canonicalization（正規化）規則，分別作用於標頭與本文，把允許的格式差異整理後再計算。
bh= 與 b=
bh= 保存本文的雜湊值；b= 是簽章值。驗證器檢查本文雜湊及簽章。
可選的 l=
指定正規化後本文參與雜湊的位元組長度；省略時涵蓋整份正規化後本文。

sourceBody.text: 數位封條的保護範圍，是選入的標頭及依規則處理的本文資料。閱讀時一併標出 h=、c= 與是否存在 l=，就能精確描述驗證涵蓋什麼。轉寄或郵件清單若改寫受保護資料，應配合其處理流程解釋驗證結果。業務內容的查核則接續由訂單、原有聯絡管道與帳號活動完成。[DKIM 標籤與驗證：RFC 6376 §3.4、§3.5、§6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6376.html#section-3.5)
5.4 DMARC：至少一條「驗證通過且對齊」的路徑
DMARC（Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance，網域式郵件驗證、報告與一致性機制）把驗證身分連到 From 的作者網域。Alignment（對齊）就是比較這兩個網域的關係。假設：

From: receipt@coffee.example
Return-Path: <bounce@mailer.example>
可信收件端記錄 SPF pass，所檢查的是 mailer.example；DKIM pass 的 d= 是 coffee.example。From 也是 coffee.example，因此 DKIM 這條路徑同時符合「通過」與「對齊」。可以把邏輯寫成容易閱讀的式子：

DMARC 通過 =
  (SPF 通過 且 SPF 網域對齊)
  或
  (DKIM 通過 且 DKIM 簽署網域對齊)

Strict Alignment（嚴格對齊）要求比較的網域完全相同；Relaxed Alignment（寬鬆對齊）依規範判定兩者是否具有相同的 Organizational Domain（組織網域）。例如在 coffee.example 為共同組織網域的前提下，mail.coffee.example 與 coffee.example 可寬鬆對齊。實作依現行規範尋找組織網域，並非一律截取最後兩段文字。[DMARC 對齊：RFC 9989](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989.html)

網域政策 p=none 表達觀察模式；p=quarantine 表達隔離偏好；p=reject 表達拒收偏好。收件系統將這些偏好與自己的評估一起用於處理決策。查證與補充：RFC 9989 於 2026 年 5 月發布，取代 RFC 7489 與 RFC 9091；本課採此現行核心規範。[RFC 9989 發布資訊與政策](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989.html)
5.5 逐欄閱讀 Authentication-Results

Authentication-Results（驗證結果標頭）是收件驗證服務寫下的檢查紀錄。先確認 authserv-id（驗證服務識別）及該欄位確由可信服務產生，再解讀每個 pass 或 fail。自己的郵件管理規則、可信閘道與日誌，是確認來源的依據。[驗證結果的信任邊界：RFC 8601 §1.2、§7](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8601.html#section-1.2)

rows: mx.recipient.example
宣告產生結果的驗證服務識別；先與可信服務設定及日誌對照。
spf=pass
此次 SPF 檢查通過。
smtp.mailfrom=mailer.example
此次檢查的信封寄件網域。
dkim=pass
此次 DKIM 簽章驗證通過。
header.d=coffee.example
該 DKIM 簽章的簽署網域。
dmarc=pass
此次 DMARC 評估通過。
header.from=coffee.example
DMARC 對照的作者網域。

sourceBody.text: 把這段讀成一句完整的判斷：「可信收件服務確認代寄平台的 SPF，以及 coffee.example 的 DKIM；其中 DKIM 和 From 對齊，形成 DMARC 通過條件。」若經過轉寄，另記錄連線來源的變化與郵件內容處理，便能追查結果差異。[間接郵件流程：RFC 7960](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7960.html)

visual.caption: 圖 6｜從網域對齊讀懂 DMARC

sourceBody.text: 6｜完整例子：咖啡店使用代寄平台寄收據
以下為教學節錄，省略真實簽章與其他標頭；假設驗證結果由可信的收件系統產生：
第一步，辨識角色。畫面作者是 coffee.example，回覆流向同網域客服；退信交給 mailer.example。
第二步，閱讀各自的驗證。SPF pass 表示目前寄信來源符合 mailer.example 的政策；DKIM pass 表示 coffee.example 的簽章驗證通過。
第三步，檢查對齊。From 是 coffee.example，DKIM 的 d= 也是 coffee.example，所以 DKIM 這條路徑同時具備「通過」與「對齊」，支持 DMARC pass。SPF 使用 mailer.example，在這個例子裡負責代寄平台自身的來源檢查。
第四步，結合業務情境。如果這是你剛完成購買的收據，可以再核對訂單編號、品項與金額；若信件另要求更改匯款帳戶，就透過原先保存的客服管道確認。技術層確認網域使用，業務層確認要求內容，兩層配合形成完整判讀。
6.1 六層判斷：把傳遞、網域與業務證據接起來

rows: 傳遞路徑
哪個節點把郵件交給哪個節點？
Received 與統一時區的時間線。
可信來源
哪些紀錄來自可查核的系統？
己方 MTA、閘道設定與郵件日誌。
來源授權
此連線 IP 是否符合該網域寄送政策？
SPF 結果及所檢查的身分。
簽章驗證
簽署網域與受保護內容如何驗證？
DKIM 結果、d=、s= 與涵蓋範圍。
網域對齊
通過驗證的網域如何對應 From？
DMARC 與至少一條通過且對齊的路徑。
業務可信度
這項要求是否符合真實交易與既有流程？
訂單、交易紀錄、原有聯絡管道與帳號活動。

sourceBody.text: 技術驗證處理網域授權與簽章；業務驗證處理實際要求。像遭接管的合法帳號、或攻擊者自有的相似拼字網域，都可能具備正常的網域驗證結果；因此付款變更與登入要求，接著透過獨立管道確認。這正是 M02 與 M09 的連結：M02 建立可追溯的技術證據，M09 檢視訊息如何利用人際信任，兩者一起支持下一步決策。
7｜從足跡轉成防護：收集適量、驗證到位
對組織管理者而言，先盤點哪些系統會代公司寄信，包括客服、電子報、收據與雲端服務，再把 SPF、DKIM 和 DMARC 設定與這份清單對照。逐步測試合法寄送與轉寄流程，持續看驗證結果和報告，依組織需求調整處理政策。配合帳號多因素驗證、異常登入偵測與既有獨立確認管道，可以把網域、帳號與業務流程一起照顧好。
對足跡分析者而言，一份實用紀錄可包含：郵件來源與取得權限、取得時間與時區、原始檔或內部識別、可信收件節點、涉及的網域、SPF／DKIM／DMARC 結果、相關業務查核與下一步。保留受控原檔，分享時使用遮蔽後節錄；標頭可能含信箱地址、內部名稱或個人資訊。

Email Tracking（郵件追蹤）也會出現在足跡教材中：遠端圖片或追蹤連結被請求時，伺服器可以記錄該次請求。圖片代理、快取與預先載入會影響這些紀錄的意義，因此報告應寫清楚觀察到的是「哪個資源在何時被請求」，閱讀行為再配合收件者回覆或其他適當證據確認。本課以已取得資料離線分析；主動追蹤與測試寄信由獨立授權的練習規則規範。[Apple 郵件隱私保護的運作](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/mail-privacy-protection/)

items.title: 讀圖重點
items.body: 在授權範圍內保存合成郵件、可信驗證結果與關聯日誌，分享時遮蔽個資。

sourceBody.text: 8｜小檢核：把寄信角色與驗證串起來
合成案例：From 是 notice@shop.example；Return-Path 是 bounce@platform.example。可信收件端顯示 SPF pass（platform.example）、DKIM pass（d=shop.example），並記錄 DMARC pass。
請用幾句話說明：① 退信與畫面作者各使用哪個網域？② 哪一條驗證路徑提供與 From 的對齊？③ 如果信中要求改用新的付款帳戶，你會透過哪個既有管道確認？
選擇題：要找「自家郵件伺服器從哪個連線對象接到信」，最直接先查看哪項資料？A. 顯示名稱；B. 自家可信節點產生的 Received；C. 主旨；D. 信件簽名檔。
參考答案會隨網站教材提供。你可以先用自己的話回答，我再依你的理解補充。
8.1 延伸理解檢核：銀行來信情境
假設以下結果已確認來自公司可信收件服務。這是合成案例，供離線判讀：
問題一：SPF 與 DKIM 都通過，DMARC 卻失敗，最直接的原因是什麼？A. 通過驗證的網域與 From 未對齊；B. SPF 要求與 DKIM 使用相同 IP；C. DKIM 只允許自行寄信；D. 我想再對照一次網域。
問題二：最下面的 Received 寫著信件來自銀行。合適的下一步是什麼？A. 依該行的銀行名稱直接歸屬來源；B. 從可信收件節點開始，逐段核對該行的產生者與證據；C. 我想再檢查一次信任邊界。
問題三：你是公司資安人員。請提出兩項接下來要核對的證據，分別說明它們如何協助確認技術來源與業務可信度。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：郵件角色與驗證
paragraphs: 退信交由 platform.example 處理，畫面作者使用 shop.example。可信收件端顯示 DKIM 驗證通過，而且簽署網域 d=shop.example 與 From 的 shop.example 相同；這條路徑符合 DMARC 的驗證與對齊條件。
SPF pass 描述 platform.example 這個信封網域的寄送來源檢查。各自記下檢查對象，就容易看懂平台代寄的分工。
遇到更改付款帳戶的要求，可透過原先保存的官方電話、已知客服入口或原有負責人聯絡方式確認。以獨立取得的管道核實新收款資訊，完成技術與業務兩層查核。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：Received 與可信紀錄
paragraphs: 選 B：先查看自家可信節點產生的 Received。它記錄該節點接收郵件的連線對象與時間，適合對照自家日誌。接著逐段確認上游紀錄的產生者，再整理時間順序。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：兩種驗證通過後，還要對照哪個網域？
paragraphs: 答案是 A。SPF 通過的信封網域是 mailer.example，DKIM 通過的簽署網域也是 mailer.example；畫面 From 則是 bank.example。兩條通過的路徑都與 bank.example 未對齊，因此這份可信結果記為 DMARC fail。
可以在紙上畫三欄：From → bank.example；SPF → mailer.example；DKIM → mailer.example。先找出每個驗證結果所屬的身分，再與 From 比較。DMARC 的通過條件是至少一條「通過而且對齊」的路徑。SPF 的來源 IP 檢查與 DKIM 的簽章檢查，各自有不同工作；合法代寄可以透過對齊的信封網域或 DKIM 簽署網域配合此規則。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：從哪裡開始驗證 Received？
paragraphs: 答案是 B。先讀公司可信收件節點自己產生的 Received，對照實際連線來源與郵件日誌，再逐段往前核對。最下面那行可以先列為「較早的來源主張」，確認其寫入系統後，再給予相應的證據權重。
記憶方式是：「時間線由下往上整理；可信度從自己的收件系統往前查。」若先前節點的日誌尚未取得，就把那段列為待查證，保留原始標頭與已核實部分。若需確認實際操作人員，另依權限取得帳號與登入等紀錄。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：哪兩項證據能支持下一步判斷？
paragraphs: 第一項可以是己方郵件閘道或 MTA 日誌，搭配它產生的 Received 與 Authentication-Results。核對接收時間、連線 IP、內部郵件識別與驗證服務，確認這份結果確實屬於本封郵件，並確認外部系統把信送到哪個己方節點。
第二項可以是銀行既有官方聯絡管道及相關業務或交易紀錄。使用先前已保存、由獨立來源確認的客服或承辦窗口，核對本次要求、通知編號與交易背景；涉及付款變更時，沿用公司的覆核流程。這樣同時建立技術來源和實際業務需求的證據。
其他合理材料包括授權取得的代寄服務日誌、DKIM 簽章與當時驗證紀錄、帳號異常登入紀錄。判斷重點是寫清楚每份材料回答哪一個問題，並把技術驗證與業務確認接起來。

sourceBody.text: 9｜今天帶走的觀念
讀一封信，可以依序問四件事：誰在畫面上署名？信封如何投遞？可信系統記錄了哪些路徑與驗證？實際要求要如何確認？
這把 M02 的來源、DNS 與足跡觀念，接回 M09 的人際信任與獨立確認。下一個單元 M02-06 會延伸到 IP、ASN、Traceroute 與網路足跡，繼續整理系統之間的關係。
本課為 Email Footprinting 的一個完整單元，含郵件路徑與驗證所需子概念。技術來源以 IETF RFC、Google 與 Apple 官方說明為主；情境資料均為合成。

en.summary: Build a clear email footprint from message roles, delivery records, and domain authentication.

sourceBody.text: CEH M02-05 | Email Footprinting: Reading Delivery Paths and Domain Authentication
1 | The main idea

Email footprinting uses public contact information and original messages you are authorized to inspect to organize sending domains, mail services, delivery paths, and authentication results. Together, these clues answer: Which systems handled this message? Which domain was used? What checks did the receiving system perform?

This lesson follows M02-04 DNS: MX records help locate receiving services; now we examine the evidence left by an actual message. It also connects to M09 anti-phishing: technical checks help validate domain use and delivery, while important business requests are confirmed through an established independent channel.

Remember the division of work: the envelope routes delivery, headers describe the message, and the receiving system supplies path and authentication evidence. All examples use synthetic data and .example domains for offline reading practice.
2 | Understand email through a parcel delivery
A parcel has a shipping label on the outside and a letter inside. Email also has two layers.

The envelope carries system delivery information. In SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol), MAIL FROM supplies the return path for delivery errors, while RCPT TO identifies actual delivery recipients. The header is the set of fields at the start of the message, including the visible From, To, and Subject. The body carries text and associated content.

For example, an event platform may send a coffee shop's receipt. The visible From can be receipt@coffee.example while bounce@mailer.example handles delivery errors. Label the separate responsibilities first. Bcc provides another helpful illustration: a recipient can be in the delivery envelope while the visible To field presents a different list. [SMTP envelope and transport](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321), [message format](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5322)

A common path is: sender's mail application → submission service → one or more relay servers → recipient server → recipient's mail application. A relay is an MTA (Mail Transfer Agent), which hands the message to the next system. Webmail lets a person use a mailbox through a website. [Internet mail architecture](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5598)

Think of ports as numbered service entrances. Server-to-server SMTP commonly uses TCP 25; user submission commonly uses 587 or implicit TLS on 465. TLS (Transport Layer Security) protects data in transit. IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) lets a mail application read and synchronize a mailbox; implicit TLS commonly uses 993. Webmail usually uses HTTPS on 443. Interpret a port together with the service configuration. [TLS for mail submission and access](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8314)

visual.caption: 1 | Mail journey and two address layers
visual.description: Envelope addresses route mail; message headers present it. SMTP sends; IMAP or HTTPS reads.

items.title: How to read the diagram
items.body: Envelope addresses route mail; message headers present it. SMTP sends; IMAP or HTTPS reads.

sourceBody.text: 3 | Open the original message: each field answers a question

In browser-based Gmail, open a message you received and choose Show original from the More menu next to Reply. Other mail applications may call this View source or Full headers. Preserve the original and prepare a redacted working copy for analysis. [Gmail's official steps](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/29436?hl=en)
• From: the presented author address. A display name is the human-friendly name beside it. Read the complete address and its domain.
• Reply-To: the suggested reply destination. Customer-service, delegated-sending, and ticketing systems may use a separate address; compare it with the actual business workflow.
• To / Cc: the message's presented primary and copy recipients.
• Return-Path: the return path recorded at final delivery, useful for comparison with the SMTP envelope.
• Date: the creation date declared in the message. Retain the time zone when comparing it with receipt time.
• Message-ID: a message identifier useful for searching and correlating logs. Services may also assign their own internal message IDs; record them separately.
• Received: reception records left by delivery nodes, central to rebuilding the message route.

• Authentication-Results: checks recorded by an authentication service, often including SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. [Message fields](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5322), [authentication-result header](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8601)

Role mailboxes such as info@ and support@ on public contact pages, and department or contact details in signatures, can also reveal an organization's public footprint. Collect fields relevant to the task and separate public-page information from technical message evidence. This continues M02-02 source validation: each field retains its own source and time.
4｜Reading Received: establish trusted hops, then reconstruct chronology

Received describes reception hops. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC describe sending authorization, signing domains, and their relationship to the visible author. Separate these questions first, then connect the evidence into a clear account of the message.
4.1 Understand reception records through parcel delivery

Imagine a parcel leaving Taipei and passing through an origin station, a transfer station, and a destination station. Each station records: “At this time, I received the parcel from this previous station.” A mail server leaves similar handover records. Received is a reception field in the message header; a system that transfers messages is called an MTA (Mail Transfer Agent).

rows: Received
A reception event; identify the system that wrote it first.
from outbound.mailer.example
Information about the previous host's name; interpret it alongside the connection IP.
In this example, the connection-source IP recorded by the receiver.
by mx.recipient.example
The server recording this reception event.
The server's recorded time; +0000 is the same offset as UTC.

sourceBody.text: Once the record is established as originating from trusted mx.recipient.example, report: “At this time, this receiving server recorded a mail connection from 192.0.2.25.” That is evidence of a handover between systems. To identify the operating account or device, obtain authorized submission-service, sign-in, or endpoint records, giving each layer of the conclusion its own supporting material. [SMTP trace information: RFC 5321 §4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321.html#section-4.4)
4.2 A three-hop example: chronology and trust verification have different directions

The following synthetic message contains three reception records. All .example names and 192.0.2.x addresses are instructional. Assume the receiving organization operates mx.recipient.example and mailbox.recipient.example and can examine both systems' logs.

A receiving server adds its own Received above the existing records. Here, the top entry is at 10:00:10 and the bottom entry is at 10:00:00. [How Received is added: RFC 5321 §4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321.html#section-4.4)

rows: Reconstruct the chronology described by the records
Bottom to top, earlier to later
10:00:00 acceptance by the outbound server → 10:00:05 gateway reception → 10:00:10 internal delivery.
Verify the credibility of each segment
Start with your trusted receiver and work toward earlier hops
Check mailbox's internal reception, then mx's external connection; obtain separate provider evidence for the earlier record written by outbound.

sourceBody.text: Convert times to a common zone first. For example, 10:00:05 +0000 is 18:00:05 +0800 in Taiwan. Estimating delay between two servers also requires considering clock synchronization. Record “the difference between header timestamps” separately from “verified transport delay” for a precise analysis.
4.3 Trust boundaries: connect each record to the system that produced it

A trust boundary separates systems you can verify from externally supplied information. In this example, mx directly observed outbound's connection; an external system describes the earlier submit → outbound segment. Divide an evidence table into “corroborated with our logs” and “external record awaiting corroboration,” then complete it segment by segment.
For example, this header entry initially provides a source claim to investigate:

Verify the claim by identifying its writer and comparing the trusted reception chain with relevant service logs. An external sender may prepopulate header content before the message enters the trusted system, so record “appearance of the entry” and “verification of its origin” separately. This connects to M09 social engineering: official-looking names and familiar brands attract trust, while independent sources and system records provide a verifiable basis for that trust.

sourceBody.text: 5｜SPF, DKIM, and DMARC: three complementary checks
5.1 Think of authorized vehicles, document seals, and a storefront name

Suppose a message displays From: A Bank <service@bank.example>. From presents author information; the receiving system then checks sending authorization and signatures to connect that name with technical evidence.

rows: SPF
A list of authorized delivery vehicles
Whether the connection-source IP matches the checked domain's sending policy.
DKIM
A digital document seal
Whether the signing domain's signature and the content it covers verify consistently.
DMARC
Comparing credentials with the storefront name
Whether a domain authenticated by SPF or DKIM aligns with the From domain.

sourceBody.text: 5.2 SPF: compare a source IP with a domain's authorization list

SPF (Sender Policy Framework) lets a domain publish sending policy in DNS (Domain Name System). TXT is a DNS record type that holds text. If a delivery platform uses 192.0.2.25, an instructional policy can be written as:
mailer.example. TXT "v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.25 -all"

v=spf1 identifies the SPF version; ip4:192.0.2.25 lists an authorized IPv4 source. If preceding conditions do not match, -all produces an SPF fail result, expressing that this domain has not authorized that source. The receiver then applies its own handling policy to reject, annotate, or otherwise process the message. [SPF fail and handling: RFC 7208 §2.6.4 and §8.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208.html#section-8.4)

The receiver usually compares the current connection IP with the domain in SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) MAIL FROM, the delivery envelope's reverse-path identity. SPF also defines checks of the HELO/EHLO identity, the greeting name used in an SMTP connection. In your analysis, explicitly record “which IP, which identity, which domain, and which result,” then compare those with the visible From. [SPF identities: RFC 7208 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208.html#section-2)
5.3 DKIM: use a key pair to verify covered content
DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) uses asymmetric cryptography: the signer keeps a private key to generate a digital signature, and the receiver obtains the public key from DNS to verify it.
This excerpt shows the tags to recognize. A real signature also contains an algorithm, signature value, and other required fields:

rows: d=coffee.example
The signing domain, subsequently compared with From for alignment.
s=selector1
The selector locates a key. Here the verifier queries the DNS TXT record at selector1._domainkey.coffee.example.
h=from:to:subject:date
Lists the header names selected for this signature; From must be signed, and the verifier selects corresponding field instances according to the rules.
c=relaxed/relaxed
Canonicalization rules for headers and body respectively; they normalize allowed formatting differences before calculation.
bh= and b=
bh= holds the body hash; b= holds the signature value. The verifier checks both the body hash and the signature.
Optional l=
Specifies the number of canonicalized body octets included in hashing; omitting it covers the entire canonicalized body.

sourceBody.text: The digital seal covers selected headers and the body data processed under those rules. Recording h=, c=, and the presence of l= precisely describes the verification scope. When forwarding or mailing-list processing changes protected material, interpret the result together with that processing. Business-content checks continue through orders, established contact channels, and account activity. [DKIM tags and verification: RFC 6376 §3.4, §3.5, and §6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6376.html#section-3.5)
5.4 DMARC: at least one path that both passes and aligns

DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) connects an authenticated identity with the author domain in From. Alignment compares the relationship between those domains. Suppose:

From: receipt@coffee.example
Return-Path: <bounce@mailer.example>
The trusted receiver records SPF pass for mailer.example and DKIM pass with d=coffee.example. From also uses coffee.example, so the DKIM path both passes and aligns. Its logic can be written as:

DMARC pass =
  (SPF pass AND SPF domain aligned)
  OR
  (DKIM pass AND DKIM signing domain aligned)

Strict alignment requires the compared domains to be identical. Relaxed alignment checks whether they share an organizational domain under the specification. For example, if coffee.example is their common organizational domain, mail.coffee.example and coffee.example can align in relaxed mode. Implementations discover organizational domains using the current specification rather than simply taking the last two labels. [DMARC alignment: RFC 9989](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989.html)

The domain policy p=none expresses monitoring mode, p=quarantine expresses a quarantine preference, and p=reject expresses a rejection preference. The receiver combines these preferences with its own assessment when deciding how to handle mail. Verification and supplementation: RFC 9989 was published in May 2026 and obsoletes RFC 7489 and RFC 9091; this lesson uses that current core specification. [RFC 9989 publication information and policy](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989.html)
5.5 Read Authentication-Results field by field

Authentication-Results records checks performed by a receiving authentication service. First establish the authserv-id (authentication service identifier) and that the field was actually produced by a trusted service; then interpret pass or fail. Your mail-administration rules, trusted gateways, and logs provide that source assurance. [Authentication-result trust boundaries: RFC 8601 §1.2 and §7](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8601.html#section-1.2)

rows: mx.recipient.example
The declared authentication service identifier; compare it with trusted-service configuration and logs first.
spf=pass
This SPF check passed.
smtp.mailfrom=mailer.example
The envelope-sender domain checked here.
dkim=pass
This DKIM signature verified.
header.d=coffee.example
The signing domain of that DKIM signature.
dmarc=pass
This DMARC evaluation passed.
header.from=coffee.example
The author domain compared by DMARC.

sourceBody.text: Read this as one complete assessment: “The trusted receiving service verified the platform's SPF and coffee.example's DKIM. DKIM aligns with From, satisfying the DMARC passing condition.” If forwarding occurred, also record the changed connection source and message processing to investigate differences in results. [Indirect mail flows: RFC 7960](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7960.html)

sourceBody.text: 6 | Worked example: a platform sends the coffee shop's receipt
This teaching excerpt omits real signatures and other headers. Assume a trusted receiving system produced the results:
First, identify roles. The visible author uses coffee.example, replies go to its support address, and delivery errors go to mailer.example.
Second, read each check. SPF pass says the current source fits mailer.example's policy. DKIM pass says the coffee.example signature validated.

Third, check alignment. From uses coffee.example and DKIM d= also uses coffee.example. That DKIM path has both a successful check and alignment, supporting DMARC pass. SPF checks the sending platform's mailer.example identity in this example.

Fourth, connect the business context. For a receipt from a purchase you just made, compare the order ID, items, and amount. A request to change payment details should be confirmed through a previously saved contact channel. The technical layer validates domain use; the business layer validates the requested action.
6.1 Six layers of assessment: connect transport, domain, and business evidence

rows: Delivery path
Which node handed the message to which node?
Received and a timeline normalized to one time zone.
Trusted origin
Which records come from verifiable systems?
Your MTA, gateway configuration, and mail logs.
Source authorization
Does this connection IP match the domain's sending policy?
SPF results and the checked identity.
Signature verification
How are the signing domain and protected content verified?
DKIM results, d=, s=, and coverage.
Domain alignment
How does an authenticated domain relate to From?
DMARC and at least one passing, aligned path.
Business credibility
Does the request match the real transaction and established process?
Orders, transaction records, established contacts, and account activity.

sourceBody.text: Technical validation addresses domain authorization and signatures; business validation addresses the actual request. A compromised legitimate account or an attacker-owned lookalike domain may have normal domain-authentication results, so payment changes and sign-in requests receive a further independent-channel check. This connects M02 with M09: M02 builds traceable technical evidence, and M09 examines how messages use interpersonal trust. Together they support the next decision.
7 | Turn footprinting into protection and useful evidence

For administrators, inventory the systems sending on the organization's behalf: support, newsletters, receipts, and cloud services. Compare SPF, DKIM, and DMARC settings with that inventory. Test legitimate sending and forwarding incrementally, review results and reports, and adjust handling policy for the organization's needs. Multi-factor authentication, unusual-login detection, and established independent confirmation channels cover accounts and business processes alongside domains.

For analysts, a useful record contains message provenance and access authorization, acquisition time and zone, original file or internal identifier, trusted receiving nodes, relevant domains, SPF / DKIM / DMARC results, business checks, and next steps. Keep a controlled original and share redacted excerpts; headers can contain addresses, internal names, or personal information.

Email tracking is another footprinting topic: a requested remote image or tracking link can produce a server-side request record. Image proxies, caching, and preloading affect its interpretation. Report which resource was requested and when, then corroborate reading behavior with an appropriate recipient response or other evidence. This lesson uses offline analysis of available data; active tracking and test sending follow separately authorized exercise rules. [Apple Mail Privacy Protection](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/mail-privacy-protection/)

sourceBody.text: 8 | Small check: connect sending roles and authentication
Synthetic case: From is notice@shop.example; Return-Path is bounce@platform.example. A trusted receiver records SPF pass for platform.example, DKIM pass with d=shop.example, and DMARC pass.

Explain briefly: ① Which domains handle delivery errors and the visible author? ② Which authentication path aligns with From? ③ If the message requests a new payment account, which established channel would you use to confirm it?

Multiple choice: To identify the connection peer from which your mail server accepted a message, which evidence do you check first? A. Display name; B. Received generated by your trusted node; C. Subject; D. Message signature block.
Reference answers will accompany the website lesson. Try your own explanation first; it will help focus any follow-up teaching.
8.1 Extended understanding check: a bank-message scenario
Assume these results have been established as originating from the company's trusted receiving service. This synthetic example is for offline interpretation:

Question 1: SPF and DKIM both pass, while DMARC fails. What is the most direct reason? A. The authenticated domains do not align with From; B. SPF requires the same IP as DKIM; C. DKIM allows only self-operated sending; D. I would like to compare the domains again.

Question 2: The lowest Received entry says the message came from a bank. What is the appropriate next step? A. Attribute the source directly from that bank name; B. Start with trusted receiving nodes and verify the entry's producer and evidence segment by segment; C. I would like to review the trust boundary again.
Question 3: As the company's security analyst, name two pieces of evidence to check next and explain how they help establish technical origin and business credibility.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Mail roles and authentication
paragraphs: Delivery errors go to platform.example, while the visible author uses shop.example. The trusted receiver records a valid DKIM signature with d=shop.example, matching the From domain. That path satisfies both DMARC authentication and alignment.
SPF pass describes the sending-source check for the envelope domain platform.example. Labeling each check's subject makes the platform's delegated-sending roles clear.

Confirm a request to change payment details through a previously saved official phone number, known customer-service portal, or established contact. An independently obtained channel supports the business check alongside technical verification.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Received and trusted records
paragraphs: Choose B: start with Received generated by your trusted node. It records that node's connection peer and reception time and can be correlated with your logs. Then establish the origin of upstream records and organize their chronology.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Which domain still needs comparison after two checks pass?
paragraphs: The answer is A. The SPF-authenticated envelope domain is mailer.example, and the DKIM-authenticated signing domain is also mailer.example. The visible From uses bank.example. Neither passing path aligns with bank.example, so this trusted result records DMARC fail.

Draw three columns: From → bank.example; SPF → mailer.example; DKIM → mailer.example. Identify the identity associated with each authentication result, then compare it with From. DMARC requires at least one path that both passes and aligns. SPF checks the sending source, while DKIM checks a signature. Legitimate outsourced delivery can satisfy the rule through an aligned envelope domain or DKIM signing domain.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Where should Received verification begin?
paragraphs: The answer is B. Start with the Received produced by the company's trusted receiving node, compare the actual connection source with mail logs, and verify earlier segments in turn. Initially classify the lowest entry as an earlier source claim; give it evidence weight appropriate to the verification of its writing system.

Remember: “Build chronology from bottom to top; verify trust outward from your own receiver.” If an earlier node's logs are still unavailable, mark that segment for verification while preserving the original header and the already verified portions. Identifying an individual operator calls for separately authorized account and sign-in evidence.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Which two pieces of evidence support the next assessment?
paragraphs: First, use your mail gateway or MTA logs together with its Received and Authentication-Results. Match reception time, connection IP, internal message identifier, and authentication service to establish that the results belong to this message and identify the external-to-internal handover.

Second, use the bank's established official contact channel and relevant business or transaction records. Contact an independently verified support or account representative through previously saved details to confirm the request, notification identifier, and transaction context. For payment changes, follow the company's existing verification process. This builds evidence for both technical origin and the real business requirement.

Other reasonable materials include authorized delivery-provider logs, the DKIM signature and contemporaneous verification record, and unusual account sign-in records. The key is to state which question each item answers and connect technical validation with business confirmation.

sourceBody.text: 9 | Takeaway
Read a message through four questions: Who is presented as its author? How did the envelope route it? Which paths and checks did trusted systems record? How will the actual request be confirmed?

This connects M02 sources, DNS, and footprinting with M09 trust and independent verification. M02-06 extends the same relationship-building approach to IP addresses, ASNs, traceroute, and network footprinting.

This is one complete Email Footprinting unit, including the supporting delivery and authentication concepts. Technical sources are IETF RFCs and official Google and Apple guidance; all scenario data is synthetic.
